text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 2.8% today, bouncing back after a volatile week that saw the stock down nearly 7% from its late-October peak. The recovery came as oil prices held firm (US crude at $103/barrel, global crude at $123/barrel) and refineries operated at a healthy 92.8% capacity, supporting margins for fuel producers—the company also announced a leadership change and company update on October 29th, which may have sparked renewed interest after the initial sell-off.

The broader context: refining stocks have been caught between two crosscurrents. On one hand, tight fuel supplies (gasoline and diesel inventories remain modest at 209 million and 103 million barrels respectively) and elevated crude prices have boosted refining profits significantly in recent quarters. On the other hand, political pressure from the White House and media focus on Big Oil's earnings have created uncertainty about how long those margins will last, making investors cautious about betting too heavily on the sector near current price levels.
